google/gemini-2.5-flash.mistake: The FOL statement `¬(p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x))` is translated in the NL as `(¬p_6(x) ∨ ¬p_0(x))`. By De Morgan's laws, `¬(A ∨ B)` is equivalent to `(¬A ∧ ¬B)`. Therefore, the FOL's antecedent means 'x does not have a precise technique AND is not dedicated to perfection', whereas the natural language's antecedent means 'x does not have a precise technique OR is not dedicated to perfection'. The logical connective between the two negated conditions in the antecedent is different.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: 1) ∀x (p_13(x) ∨ p_3(x)) vs NL “Every surgeon remains calm under pressure or thinks critically.” — The FOL applies to all x, not just surgeons; should be conditional on being a surgeon (or the domain must be restricted). 2) ∀x (p_11(x) ∨ p_12(x)) vs NL “Every surgeon either has hand-eye coordination or possesses manual dexterity.” — same missing restriction to surgeons. 3) ∀x ((p_10(x) ∧ p_11(x)) → p_8(x)) vs NL “If a surgeon stays updated on research and has hand-eye coordination, then they can perform complex procedures.” — missing surgeon restriction. 4) ∀x (p_9(x) → (p_2(x) ∧ p_1(x))) vs NL “All surgeons who develop innovative methods are meticulous and strive for excellence.” — NL restricts to surgeons who develop innovative methods; FOL does not include the surgeon predicate. 5) ∀x (p_8(x) → (p_6(x) ∨ p_9(x))) vs NL “Every surgeon who performs complex procedures either has a precise technique or develops innovative methods.” — missing surgeon restriction. 6) ∀x ((p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x)) → p_7(x)) vs NL “For all surgeons, if they have a precise technique or are dedicated to perfection, then they achieve successful outcomes.” — missing surgeon restriction. 7) ∀x (¬(p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x)) → ¬p_7(x)) vs NL “if x does not have a precise technique or is not dedicated to perfection, then x does not achieve successful outcomes.” — FOL antecedent is ¬(p_6 ∨ p_0) which is equivalent to (¬p_6 ∧ ¬p_0), but NL states (¬p_6 ∨ ¬p_0). These are not equivalent. Overall these mismatches make the set incorrect.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake:
The formulas using ∀x but whose NL says “Every surgeon …” are mismatched because the FOL lacks a Surgeon(x) antecedent. Specifically:
- ∀x (p_13(x) ∨ p_3(x)) was rendered as “Every surgeon remains calm under pressure or thinks critically.” The correct FOL (if intended only for surgeons) should be ∀x (Surgeon(x) → (p_13(x) ∨ p_3(x))).
- ∀x (p_11(x) ∨ p_12(x)) was rendered as “Every surgeon either has hand-eye coordination or possesses manual dexterity.” It should be ∀x (Surgeon(x) → (p_11(x) ∨ p_12(x))).
- ∀x ((p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x)) → p_7(x)) was rendered as “For all surgeons, if they have a precise technique or are dedicated to perfection, then they achieve successful outcomes.” It should be ∀x (Surgeon(x) → ((p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x)) → p_7(x))) or equivalently ∀x (Surgeon(x) ∧ (p_6(x) ∨ p_0(x)) → p_7(x)).

If the domain is implicitly restricted to surgeons, then these are acceptable; otherwise the omission of Surgeon(x) is an error.
